plan: This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: I exit at my bid, and if I win, I pay the second-highest bid. Bidding my true value ($30) is a weakly dominant strategy - if I bid higher, I risk paying more than my value; if I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I'd profit from. Since values are independently drawn and this is a one-shot game, truthful bidding maximizes my expected profit.

This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my exit price is determined by my own sealed bid. Since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, my dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value ($28). Bidding higher risks overpaying (winning at a price above my value), while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Truthful bidding maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies.

This is effectively a second-price sealed-bid auction (the winner pays the second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher risks overpaying if I win with a low value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $24, I should bid exactly $24 to ensure optimal outcomes in this one-shot game.
